name: zc_dusk_shape

tests.name: all three dusk knobs exist in the RUNNING build, proven by sentinel round-trip

detail.note: a cvar that does not exist reads 0.0, which is the shipped default of two of these three -- so a stale DLL would otherwise pass every readback and the run would measure an unchanged world for no visible reason. This editor was five minutes too old once already today

tests.name: the camera can actually SEE the ground it is about to measure

detail.note: THREE INDEPENDENT TESTS, because the previous single test passed on a camera buried in a bush for 32 readings. A VISIBILITY trace to the real ground point catches an occluder the colour misses; green dominance catches one the trace misses; and an upward trace FROM THE GROUND PATCH proves the ground being measured is open to the sky, which is the only form of that question a skylight experiment cares about. A frame is also captured before any reading, because the only thing that would have caught the last run in five seconds was opening one

tests.name: every arm the sweep asked for produced a reading
the pawn is at the spot at every reading, not just when it was placed
every reading agrees with itself on the luma it measures
the approved night is unchanged at the most aggressive setting the knobs allow

detail.note: GREEN: TwilightBand is exactly 0 from 18:50 down, so Shape is exactly 0 and neither term can reach these hours at any value -- criterion 4 holds structurally and not by tuning. RED: the structural argument is wrong and this approach is dead as designed

tests.name: noon is unchanged at the most aggressive setting the knobs allow
the knobs move light, not exposure -- both arms grade identically at every hour

detail.note: a non-numeric reading here is a BROKEN INSTRUMENT, not a pass: it means criterion 3 has no evidence in this run rather than that exposure held still

tests.name: exactly one directional light casts a shadow at EVERY hour measured here, night included

detail.note: OBSERVATIONAL, not a new requirement. zc_shadows S01 samples only after begin play, which is daytime, so a RED here is a long-standing fact this job is the first to be in a position to see -- not a regression caused by these knobs. Reported either way

tests.name: DuskMoonDamp actually changes the picture, so a null result below would mean something

detail.note: this is the arm that removes the moon flood. If it moves nothing, the knob is dead and every reading in the sizing sweep is a measurement of an unchanged world

tests.name: DuskSkyBoost actually changes the picture across its swept range
a continuous sky term reaches the approved night's own ground readability at both dusk hours

detail.note: GREEN: the dense ladder is worth running at the chosen setting. RED is NOT a failed job -- it is the measured tradeoff the founder asked for in place of a forced solution. But read `conclusion` before reporting it: a red because the sweep ran out of room is a fact about this job, and a red with headroom left is a fact about Wonderland. Only the second one answers the founder's question
